- **Before firing a blocking question to the human, check whether the answer is already decided.** By a rule already loaded in context, by state one read away (a sibling's config, a file already fetched), or by the presented "recommended" option simply being the status quo — each of those answers the question for free. Batch every open decision a run will need into one question rather than asking serially; a blocking prompt costs real wall-clock idle time on every round trip.
- **A bare `wait` issued in its own tool call waits on nothing.** Each shell invocation from an agent harness is typically a fresh process, so a job started with a background flag in one call leaves no job table entry for a `wait` issued in a *later*, separate call — it returns immediately, having waited on nothing, while reading in the transcript exactly like a real wait. Consume a backgrounded command's result in the same call that started it, or through the harness's own background-result mechanism — never a `wait` on its own in a subsequent call.
- **An until-loop whose condition is satisfiable on the very first check is a blind sleep wearing a disguise.** `until [ "$(date +%s)" -gt "$(date +%s)" ]; do sleep N; done`, or any variant built to always evaluate true immediately, sleeps once and returns — the exact behavior a harness's blind-sleep guard exists to block, just spelled as a loop instead of a bare `sleep`. Write the condition to test the actual state being awaited (a file's arrival, a run's status), and sanity-check it by construction: for a genuinely still-pending condition, the loop must be able to iterate more than once.
- **Resolve one wait through exactly one mechanism, never two in parallel.** Pairing a background timer with direct polling of the same condition means the wait resolves via whichever finishes first — usually the poll — and the timer's own completion then arrives later as a stray notification the session has to recognize and discard as noise, or worse, mistake for new information. Pick a background timer *or* direct polling for a given wait, not both.

 - **When an action you take kicks off an async downstream process whose output matters to what happens next (a merge triggering a build/publish/deploy), don't report the task done until that process completes and its output exists — poll for it.** Reporting at the trigger point races the async process: a follow-up action taken right after (e.g. "now ship this") would then operate on the stale prior output instead of the one just triggered.
 - **In a multi-stage agent pipeline, every failure exit must converge to the same human-triage state.** A setup-phase failure (page download, authentication, scaffolding) that posts a comment but leaves the original trigger label in place makes the item look unprocessed rather than blocked, defeating the escalation mechanism. Treat every failure mode — pre-agent setup, agent bail, post-agent quality check — as equivalent from the triage perspective: all must resolve to the same visible state (e.g. a comment naming what failed, plus the trigger label removed).
+- **A dispatched subagent's "completed" notification means its *turn* ended, not that its task did.** If the subagent itself started a background wait (its own poll loop) and its turn ended there, the final text handed back can be a placeholder ("waiting for X to report completion") rather than the real result. Read the subagent's actual final text before treating "completed" as done; if it's a placeholder, send it a follow-up message asking for its real status rather than assuming the notification itself is the report — and hand it any answer you've already independently found, rather than let both sides re-derive the same state.
+- **Before firing a blocking question to the human, check whether the answer is already decided.** By a rule already loaded in context, by state one read away (a sibling's config, a file already fetched), or by the presented "recommended" option simply being the status quo — each of those answers the question for free. Batch every open decision a run will need into one question rather than asking serially; a blocking prompt costs real wall-clock idle time on every round trip.
+- **A bare `wait` issued in its own tool call waits on nothing.** Each shell invocation from an agent harness is typically a fresh process, so a job started with a background flag in one call leaves no job table entry for a `wait` issued in a *later*, separate call — it returns immediately, having waited on nothing, while reading in the transcript exactly like a real wait. Consume a backgrounded command's result in the same call that started it, or through the harness's own background-result mechanism — never a `wait` on its own in a subsequent call.
+- **An until-loop whose condition is satisfiable on the very first check is a blind sleep wearing a disguise.** `until [ "$(date +%s)" -gt "$(date +%s)" ]; do sleep N; done`, or any variant built to always evaluate true immediately, sleeps once and returns — the exact behavior a harness's blind-sleep guard exists to block, just spelled as a loop instead of a bare `sleep`. Write the condition to test the actual state being awaited (a file's arrival, a run's status), and sanity-check it by construction: for a genuinely still-pending condition, the loop must be able to iterate more than once.
+- **Resolve one wait through exactly one mechanism, never two in parallel.** Pairing a background timer with direct polling of the same condition means the wait resolves via whichever finishes first — usually the poll — and the timer's own completion then arrives later as a stray notification the session has to recognize and discard as noise, or worse, mistake for new information. Pick a background timer *or* direct polling for a given wait, not both.

---RULES.md current---
     1	# Node.js
     2	
     3	Portable, project-agnostic practices for working in Node.js / npm codebases — package management, scripts, module resolution, runtime gotchas — true for any Node project read cold.
     4	
     5	## Module resolution
     6	
     7	- **A *named* import from a package's CommonJS entry can silently yield `undefined`.** Node recovers named bindings from a CJS module by static analysis, and that analysis fails on plenty of real entry points (a re-export built at runtime, a conditional assignment) — with no error: the import resolves, the binding is `undefined`, and the failure surfaces later as "x is not a function". When a package ships both entries, import the **ESM** one explicitly (`…/package/index.mjs`, or the `import` condition of its `exports`) for named bindings; when it doesn't, `import pkg from '…'` and destructure off the default. Resolve the package's own directory (`$(npm root -g)/<pkg>` for a global install) rather than hardcoding an absolute path into a version-pinned layout, which moves under you on the next image or upgrade.
     8	- **Modern Node (22.7+) detects ES-module syntax in a `.js` file on its own** — no `"type": "module"`, no flag, no warning. A directory of ES modules therefore needs **no `package.json` of its own** just to be loadable; adding one to declare module-ness is cargo cult, and one already present for that reason is vestigial. (Prefer `.js` consistently within a tree over mixing in `.mjs` for the same purpose; the extension is then a style choice, not a signal.)
     9	- **A throwaway script that needs a project dependency (e.g. `jsdom`) can't live in a scratchpad outside the repo.** Node's module resolution walks up the directory tree from the script's own location, and a scratchpad directory external to the project never reaches its `node_modules` — the script fails with `Cannot find module` however correctly the dependency is installed in the repo. A one-off script that needs a real dependency has to live inside the project tree instead (a gitignored scratch subdirectory works, cleaned up before committing).
    10	
    11	## Test discovery
    12	
    13	- **`node --test` skips dot-directories, so a bare invocation over a suite living under one runs
    14	  zero tests and exits green.** Node's default discovery walks the tree but ignores hidden
    15	  directories outright, and finding nothing is *success* — a run reporting no failures because it
    16	  found no tests reads exactly like a passing suite. Any CI step or local command meant to exercise
    17	  tests under a dot-path must pass that path (or an explicit glob) as an argument, and whoever adds
    18	  the step confirms it by watching the **test count be non-zero**, never by watching it go green.
    19	  Naming a path is not enough — the argument must **resolve to files that exist**: a typo'd
    20	  glob, a moved fixture or a renamed directory produces the identical zero-test green, so the
    21	  property to assert is that every path a `node --test` invocation names still matches something
    22	  in the tree.
    23	
    24	## jsdom diverges from a real browser in ways a green test can hide
    25	
    26	Two that recur:
    27	
    28	- **`body.innerText` is null in jsdom.** Code reading `el.innerText || el.textContent` therefore falls through to `textContent` under test, which *includes* the `<script>` / `<style>` text, `<select>` / `<option>` text, and CSS-hidden text a real browser's `innerText` omits. Treat body-text results as jsdom-optimistic; never add a test that only passes because of it. (1)
    29	- **`runScripts: "outside-only"` (the default) parses `<noscript>` into live DOM — the opposite of a real browser.** A `textContent` read looks clean under test but splices the `<noscript>` markup into the value in Chrome, which keeps `<noscript>` as raw text. Parse a script-free fragment with `runScripts: "dangerously"` to reproduce the browser. (2)

input.new_string:

# Node.js

Portable, project-agnostic practices for working in Node.js / npm codebases — package management, scripts, module resolution, runtime gotchas — true for any Node project read cold.

## Module resolution

- **A *named* import from a package's CommonJS entry can silently yield `undefined`.** Node recovers named bindings from a CJS module by static analysis, and that analysis fails on plenty of real entry points (a re-export built at runtime, a conditional assignment) — with no error: the import resolves, the binding is `undefined`, and the failure surfaces later as "x is not a function". When a package ships both entries, import the **ESM** one explicitly (`…/package/index.mjs`, or the `import` condition of its `exports`) for named bindings; when it doesn't, `import pkg from '…'` and destructure off the default. Resolve the package's own directory (`$(npm root -g)/<pkg>` for a global install) rather than hardcoding an absolute path into a version-pinned layout, which moves under you on the next image or upgrade.
- **Modern Node (22.7+) detects ES-module syntax in a `.js` file on its own** — no `"type": "module"`, no flag, no warning. A directory of ES modules therefore needs **no `package.json` of its own** just to be loadable; adding one to declare module-ness is cargo cult, and one already present for that reason is vestigial. (Prefer `.js` consistently within a tree over mixing in `.mjs` for the same purpose; the extension is then a style choice, not a signal.)
- **A throwaway script that needs a project dependency (e.g. `jsdom`) can't live in a scratchpad outside the repo.** Node's module resolution walks up the directory tree from the script's own location, and a scratchpad directory external to the project never reaches its `node_modules` — the script fails with `Cannot find module` however correctly the dependency is installed in the repo. A one-off script that needs a real dependency has to live inside the project tree instead (a gitignored scratch subdirectory works, cleaned up before committing).

## Test discovery

- **`node --test` skips dot-directories, so a bare invocation over a suite living under one runs
  zero tests and exits green.** Node's default discovery walks the tree but ignores hidden
  directories outright, and finding nothing is *success* — a run reporting no failures because it
  found no tests reads exactly like a passing suite. Any CI step or local command meant to exercise
  tests under a dot-path must pass that path (or an explicit glob) as an argument, and whoever adds
  the step confirms it by watching the **test count be non-zero**, never by watching it go green.
  Naming a path is not enough — the argument must **resolve to files that exist**: a typo'd
  glob, a moved fixture or a renamed directory produces the identical zero-test green, so the
  property to assert is that every path a `node --test` invocation names still matches something
  in the tree.

Two that recur:

- **`body.innerText` is null in jsdom.** Code reading `el.innerText || el.textContent` therefore falls through to `textContent` under test, which *includes* the `<script>` / `<style>` text, `<select>` / `<option>` text, and CSS-hidden text a real browser's `innerText` omits. ## Cap *and* qualify every list/search call — an unbounded one blows the tool-result limit

A list or search API call that isn't bounded returns a full page of full-bodied records and overruns the agent's tool-result cap, which costs two or three further calls to dig the answer back out of the spilled result — a pure-overhead round trip on a call whose wanted answer was a single record. Two independent bounds, both needed:

- **Qualify the query so it matches what you mean.** A bare string handed to an issue/PR search is a *full-text* search over the whole repo — title, body, and comments — so a lookup for one known issue returns every issue that merely mentions the phrase, each with its whole body. Anchor it to the field (`in:title "<exact title>"`), or use the narrower tool (a label-filtered `list_issues`, a run-id or head-SHA query) instead of a search.
- **When you already know the exact title, don't search at all — list and match it yourself.** Field anchoring is a *GitHub search API* feature, and an MCP layer in front of it may match **semantically** instead, ranking by resemblance and honouring no qualifier: the title you named can then rank below unrelated issues or be absent from the page entirely, and `in:title` changes nothing. Enumerate with `list_issues` (a narrow field list, a large page size, no state filter — a log issue is often deliberately closed) and compare the string in-session. Reserve search for what it is good at: finding items you can only *describe*.
- **Trim the fields, not just the page size.** The per-object field set is what governs the payload, so capping the page can leave the response byte-identical — measured, the same call at two page sizes returned output identical to the character. Ask for the fields you need (`["number","title","state"]` covers most lookups); dropping the body alone is usually the whole difference. Where a tool offers no field selection, narrow the query instead, or take the overflow as the answer and read the spilled result file directly rather than retrying it smaller.
- **Pass a small explicit page size.** Default page sizes are tuned for a browser, not a tool result; when the answer wanted is one issue or one run, ask for 5–10, never a bare unpaged call.

All of them, not one: a qualified query still returns a full page, a small page of unqualified matches is still the wrong records, and a small page of full-bodied records still overruns the cap.

+

+
+GitHub's code-search index can lag behind what's actually on a branch, so a search meant to find

+error, just fewer hits than actually exist. When the task needs a complete list (which repos

+
+A subscribed PR's merge or CI status change reaches the session as an activity event almost
+immediately; an unsubscribed one only gets noticed on the next manual re-poll. Subscribing a
+sample and polling the rest wastes calls re-checking PRs that would have reported themselves, and
+under-serves the ones left unsubscribed. When a run's output is more than one open PR the owner
+still has to act on, subscribe every one before ending the session.

+the fix is a plain `git commit --amend` on that commit (or the latest one, if it's still the only
+commit) to add the reference, then `git push --force-with-lease` — never `git filter-branch` or an
+equivalent rewrite across every commit on the branch to backdate the reference into each one. The
+check only needs the reference to exist somewhere reachable; a full-branch rewrite is needless risk
+(a bad regex, a bad force-push) for no benefit over the one-line fix.
+

+
+Creating a PR carries a standing instruction to search for a template first
+(`pull_request_template.md`, `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/`); a repo that genuinely has none
+pays that search's full cost on every single PR if the search is repeated each time. Once you've
+confirmed a repo carries no template, skip the search on later PRs in that same repo and write the
+body straight from the commit/issue; if it's a repo you work in repeatedly, note the absence in
+that repo's own docs so a future session doesn't re-probe either.

- **Handing the owner a command block to paste directly into their terminal** — carry no

  a pasted line ending in a comment there fails or behaves unexpectedly. Put the explanation in
  prose around the block instead of inline.

## Widget tests and goldens

- **Load real fonts before any golden** — the test binding defaults to the glyph-less Ahem stub
  (text renders as boxes). Parse `FontManifest.json` from the root bundle and `FontLoader` every
  family (strip the `packages/<pkg>/` prefix so plain family names resolve), which also loads
  MaterialIcons; bundle text faces (e.g. Roboto) in the test package's pubspec. Watch for styles
  that don't inherit the theme's family — `ButtonStyle`/`styleFrom` text styles are the classic
  leak; pin `fontFamily` there explicitly.
- **Never `pumpAndSettle` around indeterminate progress indicators** — they schedule frames
  forever and the call never returns. Use fixed-duration pumps (`pump()` then
  `pump(Duration(...))`); this also makes an in-flight state (a spinner mid-send) a deterministic,
  golden-capturable frame. Corollary: after `tap()`, pump **twice** — one frame applies state, the
  fixed-duration pump advances implicit animations (ink ripples, color lerps) past the capture.
- **Anything that fetches must be injectable**: map tile providers, avatar images. Widget tests
  block real HTTP (a 400-returning stub client), so a `NetworkImage`/network `TileProvider` in the
  tree means error boxes, not screenshots. Provide a deterministic in-memory substitute (a
  canvas-drawn `ImageProvider` works and needs no asset files).
- **Fix the viewport per suite**: set `tester.view.physicalSize` and `devicePixelRatio` to one
  phone-shaped size (and reset in teardown) so layout — and therefore goldens — can't drift with
  the harness default.
- **Async lifecycle guards need an epoch counter.** A `start()` that awaits (permission check,
  first fix) can re-arm streams/timers after `stop()`/dispose ran mid-await; bump an epoch in
  `stop()` and bail after every await if it changed. The symptom (leaked GPS subscription after
  sign-out) is invisible in tests that don't await realistically.

# Flutter

Portable, project-agnostic practices for Flutter / Dart codebases — true for any Flutter project
read cold. Earned in missingbulb/ShoutsAndWhispers (a Firebase-backed, location-driven app with an
executable-requirements UI suite); keep anything project-specific in the consuming repo's docs.

## Architecture: ports out of the widget tree

- **Widgets depend on ports, never on plugins.** Every platform/backend concern (location, auth,
  push, backend calls, the clock) enters the UI as a hand-written abstract interface with pure-Dart
  value types; plugin adapters (`geolocator`, `firebase_*`, `google_sign_in`, …) implement them and
  are constructed **only** in `main.dart`. A plugin type leaking into a screen (a geolocator
  `Position`, a `FirebaseFunctionsException`) is a defect: it silently couples every widget test to
  the plugin's platform channels.
- **Enforce the boundary with a committed import-scan test** (dart:io over `lib/ui/`, `lib/screens/`
  looking for forbidden import prefixes). The analyzer won't stop a convenient leak.
- **Ship the fakes in the package** (`lib/testing/`): scripted fakes for each port that also
  *record* what the UI asked of them, plus a `FakeWorld` bundling them with a pinned clock and the
  real app shell. Both the app's own tests and any sibling test package (e.g. an
  executable-requirements suite) import one fake world — never two parallel ones.
- **Extract the root shell into a widget** (`lib/app.dart`) taking the ports as parameters, used
  identically by `main.dart` (adapters) and the test harness (fakes). Tests must never rebuild a
  parallel MaterialApp — actuals come from the shipped shell.
- **Inject the clock.** Any widget that formats or compares times takes a `Clock` port; relative
  time rendered from `DateTime.now()` is untestable and drifts goldens.

## Widget tests and goldens

- **Load real fonts before any golden** — the test binding defaults to the glyph-less Ahem stub
  (text renders as boxes). Parse `FontManifest.json` from the root bundle and `FontLoader` every
  family (strip the `packages/<pkg>/` prefix so plain family names resolve), which also loads
  MaterialIcons; bundle text faces (e.g. Roboto) in the test package's pubspec. Watch for styles
  that don't inherit the theme's family — `ButtonStyle`/`styleFrom` text styles are the classic
  leak; pin `fontFamily` there explicitly.
- **Never `pumpAndSettle` around indeterminate progress indicators** — they schedule frames
  forever and the call never returns. Use fixed-duration pumps (`pump()` then
  `pump(Duration(...))`); this also makes an in-flight state (a spinner mid-send) a deterministic,
  golden-capturable frame. Corollary: after `tap()`, pump **twice** — one frame applies state, the
  fixed-duration pump advances implicit animations (ink ripples, color lerps) past the capture.
- **Anything that fetches must be injectable**: map tile providers, avatar images. Widget tests
  block real HTTP (a 400-returning stub client), so a `NetworkImage`/network `TileProvider` in the
  tree means error boxes, not screenshots. Provide a deterministic in-memory substitute (a
  canvas-drawn `ImageProvider` works and needs no asset files).
- **Fix the viewport per suite**: set `tester.view.physicalSize` and `devicePixelRatio` to one
  phone-shaped size (and reset in teardown) so layout — and therefore goldens — can't drift with
  the harness default.
- **Async lifecycle guards need an epoch counter.** A `start()` that awaits (permission check,
  first fix) can re-arm streams/timers after `stop()`/dispose ran mid-await; bump an epoch in
  `stop()` and bail after every await if it changed. The symptom (leaked GPS subscription after
  sign-out) is invisible in tests that don't await realistically.

## Toolchain habits

- **Verify plugin APIs against the installed source, not memory.** Major Flutter plugins break
  their APIs often (google_sign_in v7's `authenticate()`, flutter_map v7+'s options, geolocator's
  settings objects); resolved versions live in the pub cache
  (`~/.pub-cache/hosted/pub.dev/<pkg>-<ver>/lib/`) — read them before writing against them.
- **`pubspec.lock` moving without `pubspec.yaml` moving is version skew, not a dependency change.**
  An app commits its lockfile (only a *library* package gitignores it), so the file is tracked on
  purpose — the thing to keep out of the diff is the churn a local `flutter pub get` produces when
  the installed SDK resolves differently from CI's. Unless you deliberately ran an upgrade, revert
  it: `git checkout -- pubspec.lock`.
- **`flutter analyze` at zero issues** (infos included) is the bar a suite holds; lints that fight
  a deliberate convention (e.g. `file_names` vs. leaf-id case filenames) get disabled narrowly in
  that package's `analysis_options.yaml` with the reason as a comment.
- **Sandboxed/CI runners**: `flutter test` can stall for minutes at teardown on GPU-less containers
  with dropped sockets. The pattern that holds: stream output, kill the process group the moment
  the definitive marker prints (`All tests passed!` / `Some tests failed`), watchdog-kill on output
  silence. On healthy machines plain `flutter test` is equivalent — keep the wrapper thin.
- **The web sandbox ships no Flutter SDK.** Claude Code on the web boots without Flutter, so tests,
  `flutter analyze`, and golden regen can't run until it's installed. Install belongs in the
  environment **image** (built once, snapshotted, reused) — never a per-session hook that reinstalls
  every start. This pack declares that need in its `env` block ([pack.mjs](pack.mjs)); a project pastes
  one generic `environment-setup-command.sh` that runs every active pack's requirement via
  [engine/pack_loader/env-requirements.mjs](../../engine/pack_loader/env-requirements.mjs) and asserts it at session start (see [bootstrap.md](../../bootstrap.md)
  Part 9).

# web-speech pack

Active when a browser speech API — `webkitSpeechRecognition` / `SpeechRecognition`, `speechSynthesis` / `SpeechSynthesisUtterance`, or `chrome.tts` — is referenced in JS/TS source. Portable runtime gotchas for browser voice I/O (speech-to-text and text-to-speech).

Most gotchas are runtime browser behaviours with no repo-state signature a static check could read, so they live as prose (`RULES.md`). The two that **do** have a file-scoped signature are the [`web-speech-io`](skills/web-speech-io/SKILL.md) skill's check-the-work rules, which run at every Stop and in CI — each failure message is the rule.

Some of these APIs are extension-only, and where a rule touches MV3 service-worker or content-script mechanics this pack owns the speech-API facet of it specifically — never the general extension gotcha underneath.

## Rules (`RULES.md`)

| Rule | Severity | Reason | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|---|
| The recognizer owns its microphone capture | high | correctness | prose: 99 words + skill check (`web-speech-capture-released-on-pagehide`) |
| Read the whole n-best list | medium | correctness | prose: 34 words |
| Settle the listen cycle exactly once | high | correctness | prose: 47 words |
| A missing isFinal means final | high | correctness | prose: 35 words |
| Classic recognition streams to the cloud | critical | legal | prose: 74 words |
| Biasing works only on-device | medium | correctness | prose: 71 words |
| Map error names to a small taxonomy | medium | complexity | prose: 48 words |
| A missed endpoint needs a pause watchdog | high | correctness | prose: 82 words |
| Mic permission is per-origin | high | correctness | prose: 93 words |
| Prefer chrome.tts over speechSynthesis | medium | correctness | prose: 58 words |
| Relay chrome.tts from a content script | high | correctness | prose: 66 words + skill check (`web-speech-no-window-api-in-service-worker`) |
| An empty getVoices() means not-ready | high | correctness | prose: 44 words |
| Don't trust the default voice | low | correctness | prose: 39 words |
| Resolve speak() on any terminal event | high | correctness | prose: 60 words |
| Neither engine reliably supports SSML | low | correctness | prose: 37 words |

Distilled from `missingbulb/CrosswordChat` — a Chrome extension that solves the NYT crossword conversationally (voice in, voice out). Grounded in its `extension/src/speech/` ports (`stt-port.js`, `tts-port.js`, `remote-tts-port.js`, `biasing.js`), the service-worker TTS relay (`extension/src/background/service-worker.js`), and its `dev/docs/FEASIBILITY.md` speech-API analysis.

# Version history

Records for `packs/basics/pack.mjs`'s `version` field, one row per bump — added going forward from
the version this file was introduced beside (60821.4); earlier bumps are not backfilled.

| Version | Date | What changed |
|---|---|---|
| 60902.1 | 2026-09-02 | Two engineering-practice/harness-contract bullets: patch a hand-maintained JSON config as anchored text, never a `JSON.parse`/`JSON.stringify` round-trip; and a command block handed to the owner to paste into an interactive terminal carries no trailing `#` comment — interactive zsh's default doesn't honour it (#1584). |
| 60901.4 | 2026-09-01 | The pack adopts the references convention: `references.md` carries the incident evidence behind `verify-in-production` (#1121, #1460, the queue-park and label incidents), `do-later` (#1160), `writing-tests` (#429, #310, the hostname-apex case) and the `declared-check-spec-keys` check, and those prose files end the migrated rules with bare `(n)` markers instead of inline issue ids (#1564). |
| 60901.3 | 2026-09-01 | `authoring-agent-docs` narrows to the instruction files outside a pack: the "Shape a rule so it fires" house style moves to claudinite-growth's new `writing-pack-prose` skill, which also owns the per-pack `references.md` rationale convention, and a pointer says which skill to load when the file being written lives in a pack (#1560). |
| 60901.2 | 2026-09-01 | `declared-check-spec-keys` reads the engine's vocabulary through a namespace import and a capability guard: the pack lane delivers nightly and the engine lane only on a release, so this file spends a window beside an engine with no `unplacedSpecKeys` to export — and a named import of an absent export is a link-time error the loader records as a fault, which fails the self-test and parks the converge. On such an engine the rule is inert, which is the behaviour that engine already has (#1400). |
| 60901.1 | 2026-09-01 | `declared-check-spec-keys` — a declared check's key that the engine's vocabulary cannot place is now dropped at load and reported by this rule rather than thrown on, so a declaration written for a newer engine loads (with the unknown key inert) instead of dropping every rule in its file and wedging the member's converge. Advisory, because in a member the key is as likely to be skew as a typo; the canon overrides it to blocking, where engine and declarations ship from one commit (#1400). |
| 60831.6 | 2026-08-31 | `verify-in-production` gains the coded form (#1530): a URL-readable artifact files declarative `Live-probe:`/`Verify-probe:` lines routed to `claudinite-tasks/verify-production`, judged in code Action-side — no session, no egress wall, no `Model:`. The reachability gate becomes runner routing (URL → coded, GitHub read → agentic, neither → file nothing), and a fresh coded verification is forced to run at filing time and watched reporting **not yet live**, so the probes are proven failing before the release lands. |
| 60831.5 | 2026-08-31 | `writing-handover-issues` — an issue a PERSON executes is an instrument, not a description, so its body is a checklist and nothing else, with every explanation (what each step buys, what breaks while it is undone) below the last box rather than between them. Each box is one imperative line carrying the deepest URL that lands on the screen rather than a settings breadcrumb, and a step that produces a value names the control that mints it and where on that screen it appears. `verify-in-production`, `writing-migration-plans` and lifecycle's `adopt-pack` each re-spelled a fragment of that shape and now point here (#942). |
| 60831.4 | 2026-08-31 | The reachability gate is a filter rather than a router: an artifact the run cannot read is a reason to file nothing and say the change is unverified, and asking a person is a rare exception earned by a costly silent failure — not the fallback whenever no automatic check exists. A fleet-wide subject belongs to a routine holding fleet scope or to nobody. The same bar reaches every ad-hoc item in `RULES.md`: a marked issue asks an unattended session on this repo to do the work, and work it cannot do here parks minutes after being picked (#1520). |

184 3 Portable, project-agnostic practices for working in Node.js / npm codebases — package management, scripts, module resolution, runtime gotchas — true for any Node project read cold.
827 7 - **A *named* import from a package's CommonJS entry can silently yield `undefined`.** Node recovers named bindings from a CJS module by static analysis, and that analysis fails on plenty of real entry points (a re-export built at runtime, a conditional assignment) — with no error: the import resolves, the binding is `undefined`, and the failure surfaces later as "x is not a function". When a package ships both entries, import the **ESM** one explicitly (`…/package/index.mjs`, or the `import` condition of its `exports`) for named bindings; when it doesn't, `import pkg from '…'` and destructure off the default. Resolve the package's own directory (`$(npm root -g)/<pkg>` for a global install) rather than hardcoding an absolute path into a version-pinned layout, which moves under you on the next image or upgrade.
462 8 - **Modern Node (22.7+) detects ES-module syntax in a `.js` file on its own** — no `"type": "module"`, no flag, no warning. A directory of ES modules therefore needs **no `package.json` of its own** just to be loadable; adding one to declare module-ness is cargo cult, and one already present for that reason is vestigial. (Prefer `.js` consistently within a tree over mixing in `.mjs` for the same purpose; the extension is then a style choice, not a signal.)
554 9 - **A throwaway script that needs a project dependency (e.g. `jsdom`) can't live in a scratchpad outside the repo.** Node's module resolution walks up the directory tree from the script's own location, and a scratchpad directory external to the project never reaches its `node_modules` — the script fails with `Cannot find module` however correctly the dependency is installed in the repo. A one-off script that needs a real dependency has to live inside the project tree instead (a gitignored scratch subdirectory works, cleaned up before committing).
630 13 - **`btoa`/`atob` operate on Latin1 code units, not arbitrary Unicode text.** Calling either directly on a string containing a character beyond U+00FF (any non-Latin1 script — Hebrew, Cyrillic, CJK, most emoji) throws or silently corrupts it; the failure is invisible until real, non-ASCII data reaches it, which a Latin-only test fixture never exercises. Encode/decode as UTF-8 bytes first — `Buffer.from(str, 'utf8').toString('base64')` / `Buffer.from(str, 'base64').toString('utf8')` in Node, or a `TextEncoder`/`TextDecoder` bridge where `Buffer` isn't available — rather than calling `btoa`/`atob` on the text directly.
463 14 - **Before relying on a version-gated Node runtime feature, check what version CI actually pins** — the workflow's `setup-node` step (or equivalent), not the version installed in the sandbox you're working in. A session's own Node can be newer than CI's pin, so code that behaves correctly against the newer runtime can still fail in CI against the older one; a local green run proves nothing about the version that will actually execute the code in production.
373 33 - **`body.innerText` is null in jsdom.** Code reading `el.innerText || el.textContent` therefore falls through to `textContent` under test, which *includes* the `<script>` / `<style>` text, `<select>` / `<option>` text, and CSS-hidden text a real browser's `innerText` omits. Treat body-text results as jsdom-optimistic; never add a test that only passes because of it. (1)
354 34 - **`runScripts: "outside-only"` (the default) parses `<noscript>` into live DOM — the opposite of a real browser.** A `textContent` read looks clean under test but splices the `<noscript>` markup into the value in Chrome, which keeps `<noscript>` as raw text. Parse a script-free fragment with `runScripts: "dangerously"` to reproduce the browser. (2)

**web-speech** (from CrosswordChat/`browser-speech`)
- OS-rendered TTS (`chrome.tts`) bypasses the browser's own echo cancellation entirely, since AEC only attenuates audio the browser itself rendered — needs an application-level echo guard (e.g. compare a heard transcript against what was just spoken).

**basics** (from LaughCounter/`laughcounter`, Shepherd/`shepherd`)
- Surface a shipped build's exact version+build identity from real build metadata, not a hand-maintained constant — two builds can share a version string.

input.body:
growth-promote's central-stage run over the target members named in Context, resumed and extended after sitting unmerged: the original run's targets were ClaudiniteWebsite, CrosswordChat, EdFringeNow, GoogleCalendarEventCreator, LaughCounter, Shepherd (work item #1508); this pass adds a second window's targets — ClaudiniteCanary, ClaudiniteWebsite, CrosswordChat, EdFringeNow, hitbut, LaughCounter, Shepherd, TLDR, VascularColoring, WIP (work item #1584).

Each item below is generalized from its origin repo's local pack, deduped against the whole corpus, and routed to the pack whose territory it falls in.

**web-speech** (from CrosswordChat/`browser-speech`)
- OS-rendered TTS (`chrome.tts`) bypasses the browser's own echo cancellation entirely, since AEC only attenuates audio the browser itself rendered — needs an application-level echo guard.

**basics** (from LaughCounter/`laughcounter`, Shepherd/`shepherd`, WIP/`wip`)
- Surface a shipped build's exact version+build identity from real build metadata, not a hand-maintained constant.
- Before dropping a carried-over aggregate `GENERATED` file on "the next run recomputes it", check the recompute's own inputs cover the same historical span.
- Edit a hand-maintained JSON config as anchored text, never a parse/re-serialize round-trip.
- A command block handed to the owner to paste into an interactive terminal carries no trailing `#` comment.

**node** (from GoogleCalendarEventCreator/`gcec`, hitbut, WIP)
- A throwaway script needing a real project dependency can't live in an external scratchpad.
- `btoa`/`atob` operate on Latin1 code units and throw or corrupt non-Latin1 text.
- Check what Node version CI actually pins before relying on a version-gated runtime feature.

**flutter** (from WIP/`wip`)
- Real file or image I/O inside `testWidgets` needs `tester.runAsync`, or the test hangs in the fake-async zone rather than failing.

**git-github** (from EdFringeNow, Shepherd, GoogleCalendarEventCreator, TLDR)
- `gha/scheduled-failure-escalation` widens from `schedule:` alone to also catch `workflow_run:`/`repository_dispatch:` triggers.
- `list_pull_requests`'s `merged` field is unreliable for landed-ness; `search_code` can undercount for exhaustive enumeration; subscribe every PR a sweep leaves open, not a sample; amend rather than rewrite history for a missing issue reference; stop re-probing for a confirmed-absent PR template.
- `actions_list`'s `list_workflow_runs` can ignore `per_page` entirely — don't retry it smaller (confirmed independently on two repos).
- `issue_read`'s `get_*` methods reject a PR number outright — use `pull_request_read`.

**claudinite-growth** (`unattended-agents` skill, from EdFringeNow, Shepherd, WIP)
- A dispatched subagent's "completed" notification can carry a placeholder final message rather than its real result.
- Check whether `AskUserQuestion`'s answer is already decided before firing it.
- A bare `wait` in its own Bash call waits on nothing — each invocation is a fresh shell.
- An until-loop satisfiable on its first check is a blind sleep in disguise.
- Resolving one wait through two mechanisms at once (a background timer plus direct polling) leaves the timer's own completion as a stray notification.

Every pack touched has its `version` bumped, a `VERSIONS.md` row, and (where its RULES.md changed) an updated README rule index. `node --test` on the full suite (2936 tests) and `check_the_world.mjs` both pass clean (0 blocking).

**Notable rejections** (already covered elsewhere in the corpus): CrosswordChat's remaining `browser-speech` rules, EdFringeNow's GitHub-MCP-token-cap/CI-infra-outage/`search_issues` findings, GoogleCalendarEventCreator's CDP/jsdom/generic-extractor findings, LaughCounter's `macos-audio`/`on-device-privacy` findings, Shepherd's `git checkout -- `/exact-title-search/stale-main/`AskUserQuestion`/subagent-placeholder findings, TLDR's parallel-scratch-filename finding, VascularColoring's and hitbut's remaining local-pack content — all duplicate existing rules nearly verbatim, or (VascularColoring, ClaudiniteCanary) are product-specific with nothing portable to lift.

**Deferred to a sibling PR, not this one**: CrosswordChat's `host-page-adaptation` pack is a large, cohesive, genuinely uncovered practice ("driving a host page you don't own") that doesn't fit any existing pack's territory — already split into its own PR, #1525, per the promote task's own convention.

input.body:
**2026-09-02** — Run over #1584's target members (ClaudiniteCanary, ClaudiniteWebsite, CrosswordChat, EdFringeNow, hitbut, LaughCounter, Shepherd, TLDR, VascularColoring, WIP). Found PR #1524 and its sibling #1525 already open, unmerged since a prior run (work item #1508) whose Context overlapped 5 of these 10 members — completed #1524 in place (rebase + new content) rather than duplicating it; left #1525 untouched, it needed no new content.

Promoted, all deduped against the whole corpus first:

- **web-speech** (CrosswordChat): OS-rendered TTS bypasses the browser's own echo cancellation — application-level echo guard needed. [carried over from #1508]
- **basics**: shipped-build version+build identity from real metadata (LaughCounter) [#1508]; a carried-over aggregate `GENERATED` file's recompute-inputs must cover the same span before dropping it (Shepherd) [#1508]; edit hand-maintained JSON config as anchored text, never re-serialize (WIP); a terminal command block for the owner carries no trailing `#` comment — interactive zsh doesn't honour it by default (LaughCounter).
- **node**: a throwaway script needing a real dependency can't live in an external scratchpad (GoogleCalendarEventCreator) [#1508]; `btoa`/`atob` operate on Latin1 code units and corrupt non-Latin1 text (hitbut); check what Node version CI actually pins before relying on a version-gated feature (WIP).
- **flutter**: real file/image I/O inside `testWidgets` needs `tester.runAsync` (WIP) — genuinely new pack section, no prior coverage.
- **git-github-advanced** (skill): several EdFringeNow/Shepherd/GoogleCalendarEventCreator items [#1508]; `actions_list`'s `list_workflow_runs` can ignore `per_page` entirely — confirmed independently on EdFringeNow and TLDR, don't retry it smaller; `issue_read`'s `get_*` methods reject a PR number, use `pull_request_read` (TLDR).
- **unattended-agents** (skill): subagent-completed-is-a-placeholder and check-AskUserQuestion-already-decided (EdFringeNow/Shepherd) [#1508]; a bare `wait` in its own Bash call waits on nothing — fresh shell per invocation (EdFringeNow); an until-loop satisfiable on its first check is a blind sleep in disguise (EdFringeNow); resolving one wait through two mechanisms at once leaves a stray notification (EdFringeNow/WIP).

Left open for owner review: #1524 (this run's lessons, CI green), #1525 (CrosswordChat's `host-page-interaction` pack mint, from the prior run, untouched).

**Notable rejections** (deduped against existing coverage, confirming strong prior promotion): ClaudiniteCanary and VascularColoring had nothing portable — both are entirely product-specific (canary self-tests; vessel-image research method already generalized into the existing `research-project` pack). Most of EdFringeNow's, Shepherd's, and CrosswordChat's remaining local-pack content duplicates canon rules nearly verbatim (GitHub MCP token-cap/list-search guidance, CI-infra-outage detection, `git checkout -- `, exact-title search, macOS audio lifecycle, on-device privacy boundary, web-speech gotchas) — see PR #1524's body for the full breakdown.
